Consult Summary:
- A sexually active patient with acute lower abdominal ache and nausea, feverish sensations, and urinary frequency; pregnancy must be excluded; differential includes early pregnancy complication, UTI/pyelonephritis, PID, and ovarian cysts; plan includes expedited in-person assessment and appropriate testing.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Several days of feeling sick with lower abdominal ache and a feverish, hot/sweaty sensation. Nausea without vomiting. Symptoms present for about 2–3 days; pain described as dull and constant below the belly button.
- Timeline and progression: Onset of abdominal pain and nausea about 2 days ago, ongoing and persistent; no vomiting to date.
- Associated symptoms: Increased urinary frequency without urgency or dysuria; no foul-smelling urine; no vaginal discharge reported; no significant rectal/GI symptoms beyond constipation last week (resolved).
- Urinary symptoms: Going to the toilet more often; no pain on urination; no urinary urgency.
- GI history: Last week had constipation (now resolved); regular bowel movements yesterday.
- Gynecologic history: Last menstrual period about 3 weeks ago; currently due on period; occasional pink/tinted appearance in urine possibly related to menstrual cycle; sexually active with implants (Implanon); regular boyfriend; currently using contraception.
- Menstrual/contraception: Implant contraception (Implanon) in place; last menses ~3 weeks ago; may have light spotting; no recent vaginal bleeding described beyond possible light spotting.
- Pregnancy considerations: Uncertain pregnancy status; advised to rule out pregnancy with testing.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Medications: No regular medications documented; Implanon implant noted (no dose/route/frequency applicable).
- Social history: Lives with boyfriend; non-smoker; no alcohol use discussed.
- Family history: Brother with type 1 diabetes.
- ROS negatives/pertinent negatives: No vaginal discharge; no dysuria; no discharge; no dizziness or fainting reported.

- Contraception: Implanon implant.
- Family history notable for brother with type 1 diabetes; no other PMH documented.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
- Acute lower abdominal ache with nausea and feverish sensations in a sexually active patient with uncertain pregnancy status; top clinical consideration is early pregnancy complication (threatened abortion or ectopic), with UTIs, PID, and ovarian/cystic etiologies also on the differential. A face-to-face assessment with testing is planned to clarify diagnosis.

DDx Integration (top 2–3 aligned with transcript; conflict noted if applicable):
- Early pregnancy complication (threatened abortion or ectopic pregnancy)
  - Supporting: sexual activity, last menses ~3 weeks ago, lower abdominal ache with nausea, pink-tinged urine reported; clinician planned to rule out pregnancy.
  - Opposing: no confirmed pregnancy test result or vaginal bleeding documented yet.
- Urinary tract infection / pyelonephritis
  - Supporting: increased urinary frequency; feverish, hot/sweaty sensation.
  - Opposing: no dysuria, no flank pain, no foul urine odor documented.
- Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
  - Supporting: fever with lower abdominal pain in a sexually active patient; STI risk factors implied by sexual activity.
  - Opposing: no vaginal discharge or cervical motion tenderness described.
- Corpus luteum/functional ovarian cyst
  - Supporting: dull, constant lower abdominal ache with cyclic timing after LMP (~3 weeks); occasional light spotting could align with luteal changes.
  - Opposing: fever is not typical for a simple ovarian cyst; no imaging to confirm.

- If there is any conflict between transcript and the differential, note: conflict noted.

Issue 1: Suspected pregnancy-related condition (early pregnancy complication)
- Diagnosis/Impression: Pregnancy status uncertain; high priority to exclude pregnancy-related etiologies (threatened abortion or ectopic).
- Plan:
  - Arrange urgent in-person GP assessment today.
  - Obtain pregnancy testing (urine or serum hCG) and consider quantitative hCG as indicated.
  - If positive or concern for ectopic/pregnancy-related issues, initiate obstetric follow-up and appropriate imaging (e.g., transvaginal ultrasound) as indicated.
  - Safety netting: return sooner if worsening pain, dizziness, syncope, heavy vaginal bleeding, or fever escalation.

Issue 2: Possible UTI/Pyelonephritis
- Diagnosis/Impression: Consider urinary tract infection given frequency of urination and fever-like symptoms.
- Plan:
  - Urinalysis (and urine culture if indicated) to evaluate for infection.
  - Hydration optimization; symptomatic care as appropriate.
  - If positive or rising suspicion for pyelonephritis, escalate management per local guidelines (antibiotics and follow-up as indicated).

Issue 3: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) or ovarian pathology
- Diagnosis/Impression: PID or ovarian pathology (e.g., corpus luteum cyst) considered in the differential.
- Plan:
  - Pelvic examination as part of the in-person visit.
  - Consider pelvic ultrasound if indicated by exam or imaging.
  - STI screening as clinically appropriate.
  - If PID suspected clinically, treat according to standard guidelines and arrange follow-up.

General Plan:
- Schedule a face-to-face GP visit today for a full physical examination and targeted investigations.
- If patient’s condition worsens (fever, increasing abdominal pain, dizziness, faintness, or heavy bleeding), seek urgent care.
- Review pregnancy test results and imaging findings promptly with follow-up instructions provided at the visit.
- Continue contraception with Implanon as advised; discuss pregnancy planning or alternatives if pregnancy is desired or if concerns persist.
